analysis.title: Global Rates Trader: From Hawkish Risk to Risk-Off
key_insights: Risk-off has undone much of the earlier US-led hawkish repricing across global front-ends. GS baseline of steady growth and disinflation does not argue for sharply lower yields. It points to gradual relief as inflation progress shifts policy risks and restores bonds' hedge value.
A deeper challenge to the AI trade would change that baseline, because the AI buildout underpins broader optimism and the market's pricing of durably higher policy rates.

US: firm macro data, hawkish Fedspeak and equity turbulence have produced lower growth pricing, sustained hawkish policy pricing and a marked tightening in financial conditions. GS sees the implied policy path as too hawkish if current inflation pricing is borne out.

US trade: buy 3m5y receivers versus 3m2y receivers, weighted by implied vol (about 12.5% extra DV01 on the 3m5y leg, entry 0bp, target 15bp, stop -8bp). The case rests on 1y1y/2y1y curves flattening more than their beta in 5%+ equity drawdowns and on 2s5s flattening after rate-driven financial conditions tightening.
GS says it was stopped out of a real-rates-versus-nominals beta trade but still sees appeal in it over the medium term.

MBS index convexity fell to around zero in the autumn selloff, which reduces convexity-hedging that amplifies selloffs. Convexity is more likely to add a tailwind to duration in large rallies, and 10y-tail implied vol has historically underperformed shorter expiries after such periods.
GS sees the clearest route to higher rates vol as large rallies, because tighter policy expectations are already broadly priced and growth concerns limit sharp yield rises.

Treasury swap spreads: front-end spreads are at fair value and long-end spreads slightly wide, so there is no clear valuation case for long spread positions. Funding has been tighter since mid-October on bill supply, TGA and weak money fund demand. Some pressure has eased, and relief from constrained bill issuance is not expected until Q2.

Canada: BoC rhetoric is hawkish while data is dovish, with all core inflation metrics at or below 2% yoy. A December hike risk has risen, but GS expects hawkishness to front-load tightening rather than raise the peak. It favors front-end flatteners and 1y1y forward longs.

Europe: GS forecasts the 10y Bund at 3.10% by year-end and favors Bund longs. German front-end selling reflected spillovers from abroad rather than domestic news. Softer euro area growth into H1 2027 and sovereign spread risk should constrain selloffs in European duration.

Sovereign spreads remain near year-to-date wides despite recent tightening. Lower oil and gas prices after the US midterms and easing French political risk helped. GS expects energy relief first and political clarity only after the 2027 French and Italian elections.

UK: gilts sold off on hawkish BoE commentary and spillovers from the strong US CPI print, while domestic data softened. GS sees pricing through February as too hawkish, would receive on further selloffs, and keeps a preference for curve steepeners. The 2y OIS has disconnected from falling oil prices.

Scandinavia and Switzerland: GS expects two more Riksbank hikes to 2.5% in 2027 and keeps a SEK flattening bias. Norway's September hike to 4.5% likely marked the peak, so GS favors steeper NOK curves relative to SEK. The SNB is expected to hold at 0% through 2027.

Japan: GS expects the BoJ to hike faster than priced and the JGB curve to flatten. It adds 2s10s JGB flatteners (entry 94bp, target 75bp, stop 105bp). Risks are risk-off interrupting BoJ tightening and the late-December 2026 budget reviving fiscal concerns.

Australia and New Zealand: a weak employment report drove the sharpest one-day AUD rates rally in two years, but wages were firm and October CPI is likely energy-driven. GS prefers anchoring AUD longs in the belly and still sees value in paying February RBA OIS as a hedge. In NZ it prefers curve steepeners over outright longs.

trade_ideas.description: Long 3m5y USD receivers versus short 3m2y USD receivers, vol-weighted, about 12.5% extra DV01 on the 3m5y leg (entry 0bp, target 15bp, stop -8bp)
trade_ideas.rationale: Equity drawdowns and rate-driven financial conditions tightening have historically favored belly outperformance and curve flattening.
trade_ideas.risk: Inflation news and Fed communication may limit how much the very front end participates in rallies.

trade_ideas.rationale: GS expects the BoJ to hike faster than priced, which should contain back-end risk premium and flatten the curve.
trade_ideas.risk: Risk-off interrupting the BoJ tightening cycle or the late-December 2026 budget reviving fiscal concerns.

trade_ideas.description: Long Bunds, favorable risk-reward given softer euro area growth and lower realized volatility
trade_ideas.rationale: Bunds should outperform in global selloffs and hawkish news should deepen curve flattening, insulating the belly and longer forwards.
trade_ideas.risk: Geopolitics and risk asset performance remain important considerations for duration.

trade_ideas.description: UK curve steepeners and receiving on further gilt selloffs
trade_ideas.rationale: Cumulative BoE pricing through February is too hawkish and the 2y OIS has underperformed its beta to energy prices.
trade_ideas.risk: A December BoE hike, or a rebound in energy prices.

trade_ideas.description: Canada front-end flatteners and 1y1y forward longs
trade_ideas.rationale: Hawkish BoC impulses should front-load tightening rather than extend the peak, and labor slack is slowing non-shelter wage-sensitive inflation.
trade_ideas.risk: A sequential December BoC hike despite weak labor data.

trade_ideas.description: Steeper NOK curves relative to SEK, with a SEK flattening bias
trade_ideas.rationale: Norway's hike cycle likely peaked while Sweden is expected to hike twice more in 2027.
trade_ideas.risk: Lingering Norwegian inflation risks constrain the pace of cuts.

trade_ideas.description: Pay February RBA OIS as a front-end hedge, with AUD longs anchored in the belly of the curve
trade_ideas.rationale: Front-end pricing has run ahead of data after firm wages and an energy-driven October CPI is expected, while the broader rally has staying power on a softer growth outlook.
trade_ideas.risk: GS was stopped out of the pay February RBA recommendation.

trade_ideas.description: NZ curve steepeners over outright longs
trade_ideas.rationale: GS expects the RBNZ tightening path to underdeliver versus market pricing, with lingering inflation uncertainty.

risk_factors: A deeper challenge to the AI trade would change the baseline and could keep markets pricing higher policy rates.
Higher funding volatility, including repo pressure and cheap bills versus OIS, could challenge carry expressions in risk-off.
Fiscal uncertainty in the UK (Spending Review), France and Italy limits compression in long-end term premia and sovereign spreads.
A rebound in energy prices would remove the UK front-end relief buffer.
Japan: risk-off interrupting BoJ tightening or fiscal concerns from the late-December 2026 budget.
Australia: October CPI likely shows an energy-driven reacceleration, a fresh upside catalyst for front-end yields.
charts_described: Exhibit 1: equity drawdowns have seen a stronger tendency for forward curves to flatten more than implied by their beta to front-end rates (3m changes in 1y1y/2y1y over the last 5 years).
Exhibit 2: 2s5s shows a strong flattening tendency in the month following rate-driven FCI tightening.
Exhibit 4: 1y10y implied vol has tended to decline by more than implied by the broader surface after MBS convexity peaks around 0.
Exhibit 5: Germany has been an importer of bearish pressures from abroad amid limited hawkish domestic news.
Exhibit 6: UK front-end 2y OIS has recently disconnected from energy prices, underperforming its Brent beta.
Exhibit 7: the JGB curve slope has been directional with equities and yields abroad, which should limit steepening risk in risk-off.
vol_and_positioning: MBS index convexity is around zero after the autumn selloff, which should minimize convexity-hedging that amplifies selloffs.
Implied vol on 10y tails has tended to underperform shorter expiries after MBS convexity peaks near zero, possibly reflecting weaker demand for long vol hedges.
GS sees the clearest route to higher rates vol through large rallies rather than selloffs.
Treasury swap spread vol has been fairly low despite elevated macro risk and outright yield volatility.
GS positioning dashboard shows a US option implied position indicator score of 0, a fund positioning indicator of -2 and a data response indicator of 0.
CFTC duration-weighted positioning shows speculators net short across SFR, TU, FV, TY, TN, US and WN contracts, with asset managers net long in TU through WN.
geopolitical: Oil and gas prices fell meaningfully after the US midterm elections, easing European sovereign spread pressure.
French RN's modest shift on its pension position drew a positive reception, with OAT outperformance on November 17.
Political clarity in France and Italy is unlikely until the 2027 elections.
Japan's budget proposal in late December 2026 could revive fiscal concerns.

tension_points.bull_case: Steady growth and disinflation point to relief in yields over time as inflation progress shifts the distribution of policy risks and reinforces bonds' hedge value.
tension_points.bear_case: Deeper challenges to the AI trade would change the calculus, given the AI buildout's importance to broader optimism and to markets pricing durably higher policy rates.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A deeper challenge to the AI trade, which GS says would change its baseline of steady growth and disinflation.

tension_points.bull_case: The rally has staying power given a softer growth outlook, and AUD longs offer compelling asymmetry versus the G10.
tension_points.bear_case: Front-end pricing has run ahead of data. Wages were firm and unemployment remains below the RBA's NAIRU estimate.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Next week's October CPI showing an energy-driven reacceleration, which gives front-end yields fresh upside catalysts.

tension_points.bull_case: Hawkish impulses should front-load tightening rather than extend the peak, supporting front-end flatteners and 1y1y forward longs.
tension_points.bear_case: Hawkish commentary raises the risk of a sequential December hike despite earlier guidance to proceed carefully.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Governor Macklem's speech next week may clarify the near-term path, and GS says it may offer slightly more clarity.

tension_points.bull_case: BoJ hiking faster than priced should contain back-end risk premium and flatten 2s10s toward other G4 curves.
tension_points.bear_case: Greater risk-off or fiscal sustainability concerns could interrupt the BoJ cycle or steepen the curve.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Growth concerns interrupting the BoJ tightening cycle, or the late-December 2026 budget proposal reviving fiscal concerns. Trade stop is 105bp on 2s10s.

tension_points.bull_case: Pricing through February is too hawkish and the 2y OIS has underperformed its energy beta, leaving scope for relief.
tension_points.bear_case: A December BoE hike is a risk to the baseline of a final 25bp hike in February.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A rebound in energy prices would remove part of the relief scope, though GS says it leaves some buffer.
